newsitem.title: UK: Lanica Trust confirms Co-op approach.
newsitem.headline: Lanica Trust confirms Co-op approach.

text.p: Lanica Trust Ltd confirmed on Sunday that "a company in which it has an investment" will make an approach to Britain's Co-operative movement to "discuss the possible purchase of certain non-food businesses".

Earlier the Sunday Times, a British weekly newspaper, reported that Lanica was expected to make a 500 million pound ($820.1 million) offer for the businesses owned by the Co-Operative Retail and Co-Operative Wholesale societies.
These ranged from petrol stations, funeral parlours, chemists, opticians and department stores, the paper said.

Lanica said it was making a statement in response to press reports and that the unnamed company would "be approaching the respective chief executives of the two Co-operative companies", adding that any discussions would "take some time".

The Sunday Times said Lanica's bankers Hambros Plc would be writing to the boards of the two Co-Operative companies and that an announcement was also likely to be made to the London Stock Exchange. Neither of the Co-operative societies were immediately available for comment.

Lanica was previously known as New Guernsey Securities and changed its name when entrepreneur Andrew Regan took control last year when the stock was trading at 203p. The shares closed on Friday at 16.37 pounds.
